title: Plaintiff's Original Petition and Application for Temporary Injunction
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-56789

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
151ST JUDICIAL DISTRICT

MARGARET ELLEN HAYNES, Plaintiff
v.
TECHNOVANCE SOLUTIONS, INC., Defendant

PLAINTIFF'S ORIGINAL PETITION AND APPLICATION FOR TEMPORARY INJUNCTION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Margaret Ellen Haynes, hereinafter referred to as “Meg” or “M.E. Haynes,” Plaintiff, complaining of and against Technovance Solutions, Inc., hereinafter “Technovance,” and for cause of action would respectfully show unto the Court the following:

I. DISCOVERY CONTROL PLAN
1. Plaintiff intends to conduct discovery under Level 3 of Rule 190 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

II. PARTIES
2. Plaintiff Margaret Ellen Haynes is an individual who resides in Harris County, Texas. Her date of birth is March 14, 1980. Her Social Security number is 456-78-9123. Plaintiff is a former employee of Defendant and may be contacted via her attorney, Robert J. Caldwell, at 713-555-0148 or by email at rcaldwell@caldwellfirm.com.
3. Defendant Technovance Solutions, Inc. is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business at 2000 Innovation Drive, Houston, Texas 77002. Defendant may be served with process through its registered agent, Sarah K. Nguyen, at the same address.

III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE
4. This Court has jurisdiction over the parties and subject matter because the amount in controversy exceeds the minimum jurisdictional limits of this Court, and the cause of action arose in Harris County, Texas. Venue is proper under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 15.035 because the Defendant’s principal office is located in Harris County.

IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
5. Plaintiff was employed by Defendant from June 1, 2015, until her termination on September 30, 2024. At the time of her departure, Plaintiff held the position of Senior Software Architect. 
6. As a condition of her employment, Plaintiff executed a Non-Disclosure, Non-Solicitation, and Non-Competition Agreement (the “Agreement”) on January 15, 2015. The Agreement contained a covenant not to compete for a period of twelve (12) months following termination, restricted to a 50-mile radius of Defendant’s Houston office.
7. On October 1, 2024, Plaintiff commenced employment with a competitor, DataCore Systems LLC, located at 5000 Quantum Boulevard, Austin, Texas 78701. Plaintiff’s new role is Chief Architect, responsible for developing similar software products.
8. Defendant alleges that Plaintiff has breached the non-compete and non-solicitation provisions by using confidential information and soliciting Defendant’s clients. Plaintiff denies these allegations and asserts that the non-compete is unenforceable because it is not ancillary to an otherwise enforceable agreement, as required by Texas Business and Commerce Code § 15.50.
9. Defendant has threatened legal action and has sent cease-and-desist letters to Plaintiff and DataCore Systems LLC, causing Plaintiff irreparable harm to her professional reputation and ability to earn a livelihood.

V. CAUSES OF ACTION
10. Plaintiff seeks a declaratory judgment that the non-compete covenant is void and unenforceable because it is overbroad, exceeds the limits of § 15.50, and imposes undue hardship.
11. In the alternative, Plaintiff asserts that any restrictive covenant must be reformed to be reasonable, per the standards set forth in 
DeSantis v. Wackenhut Corp., 793 S.W.2d 670 (Tex. 1990), and 
Butler v. United States, 295 U.S. 3 (1935).

VI. TEMPORARY INJUNCTION
12. Plaintiff requests a temporary injunction prohibiting Defendant from enforcing the non-compete pending final trial. Plaintiff has no adequate remedy at law. The balance of harms favors Plaintiff, as she will suffer substantial financial and professional harm without an injunction.

VII. PRAYER
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that Defendant be cited to appear and answer, that a temporary injunction issue, and that on final hearing, Plaintiff recover all relief requested, including costs and attorney’s fees.

Respectfully submitted,

CALDWELL & ASSOCIATES
Robert J. Caldwell
State Bar No. 24051234
1000 Main Street, Suite 500
Houston, Texas 77002
Telephone: 713-555-0148
Email: rcaldwell@caldwellfirm.com

ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that a true copy of the foregoing was served on counsel for Defendant, Attorney Linda M. Park, 300 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701, on November 1, 2024.

/s/ Robert J. Caldwell
Robert J. Caldwell

title: Defendant's Answer and Counterclaim
text:
CIVIL ACTION NO. 24-8891

IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
DALLAS DIVISION

TECHNOVANCE SOLUTIONS, INC., Plaintiff
v.
MARGARET HAYNES, Defendant

DEFENDANT'S ANSWER AND COUNTERCLAIM

COMES NOW, Margaret Haynes, (also known as “Maggie Hayes” during her college years, and as “M.E. Haynes” in professional publications), Defendant, and files this Answer to the Complaint filed by Technovance Solutions, Inc. (“Technovance”), and respectfully shows:

I. ANSWER
1. Defendant admits the allegations in Paragraphs 1-3 of the Complaint, but denies the remaining allegations.
2. Specifically, Defendant denies that she breached any valid non-competition covenant. Defendant avers that the covenant is unenforceable as a matter of law under Texas Business and Commerce Code § 15.50, because it is not ancillary to a valid sale of a business or an otherwise enforceable agreement, and it overly restricts her ability to practice her profession.
3. Defendant also denies that she misappropriated any trade secrets. Any information she used was general knowledge and skill acquired during her tenure, not confidential.

II. COUNTERCLAIM
4. Defendant reasserts and incorporates the allegations above and adds the following:
5. Defendant was employed by Technovance from June 1, 2015, to September 30, 2024. Her employment was at-will. She executed an agreement on January 15, 2015, which included a non-competition clause. Defendant is now employed by DataCore Systems LLC, a competitor, in a similar role.
6. Defendant asserts a counterclaim for tortious interference with contract against Technovance. Technovance, without legal justification, contacted DataCore Systems LLC and threatened litigation, causing DataCore to suspend Defendant’s employment, thereby interfering with her valid employment contract.
7. Defendant further counterclaims for declaratory relief, seeking a declaration that the non-competition clause is void and unenforceable.

III. AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES
8. Defendant asserts the equitable defense of unclean hands, because Technovance induced her to sign the agreement through misrepresentations regarding the scope.
9. Defendant incorporates the doctrine set forth in 
REST. (3d) OF AGENCY § 1.01, which is not a case but a restatement, but also cites 
E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co. v. Christopher, 431 F.2d 1012 (5th Cir. 1970), regarding trade secret law.

IV. PRAYER
WHEREFORE, Defendant prays that Plaintiff take nothing, that Defendant recover damages on her counterclaim, and for all other relief.

Respectfully submitted,

LAW OFFICES OF HERNANDEZ & SANCHEZ
By: /s/ Carlos M. Hernandez
Carlos M. Hernandez, State Bar No. 24078456
Attorney for Defendant
500 Austin Avenue, Suite 1200
Dallas, Texas 75201
Tel: 214-555-0199
Email: chernandez@hernandezlaw.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that on November 10, 2024, a true copy of this document was served on Attorney Linda M. Park, counsel for Plaintiff, at 300 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701, via e-filing.

/s/ Carlos M. Hernandez

title: Motion to Compel Discovery
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS
353RD JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. D-1-GN-24-004536

IN RE: NON-COMPETE DISPUTE BETWEEN MARGARET HAYNES AND TECHNOVANCE SOLUTIONS, INC.

MOTION TO COMPEL DISCOVERY AND FOR SANCTIONS

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE ANDREW T. MORRISON:

COMES NOW, Plaintiff Margaret Haynes (also known as “Maggie” and as “M.E.H.”), by and through her attorney, Joseph W. Kim, and moves this Court to compel Defendant Technovance Solutions, Inc. (“Technovance”) to fully respond to discovery requests propounded on October 15, 2024.

I. BACKGROUND
1. This is an employment non-compete dispute. Plaintiff served on Defendant requests for production and interrogatories seeking, among other things, the identities of any clients allegedly solicited, and all documents relating to the alleged misappropriation.
2. Defendant has objected to nearly all requests, asserting privilege and relevance, but has provided no privilege logs.

II. ARGUMENT
3. Defendant’s objections are meritless. The requested information is directly relevant to Plaintiff’s claims and Defendant’s defenses. The Texas Rules of Civil Procedure require a privilege log; Defendant’s failure warrants sanctions.
4. In support, Plaintiff cites 
In re National Lloyds Ins. Co., 532 S.W.3d 511 (Tex. App.—Austin 2017, orig. proceeding), which holds that a party cannot assert a blanket privilege without a log.
5. Moreover, the discovery sought is essential for Plaintiff to prepare for trial, and undue delay would prejudice her. Plaintiff also cites 
In re X, 300 S.W.3d 1 (Tex. 2009) for the standard of mandamus.

III. PRAYER
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that the Court compel Defendant to respond within 10 days, award reasonable expenses, and for such other relief.

Respectfully submitted,

KIM & ASSOCIATES
By: /s/ Joseph W. Kim
Joseph W. Kim
State Bar No. 24123456
505 Congress Avenue, Suite 1500
Austin, Texas 78701
Tel: 512-555-0173
Email: jkim@kimlaw.com

CERTIFICATE OF CONFERENCE
I certify that I conferred with opposing counsel, Ms. Linda Park, on November 5, 2024, but the parties were unable to resolve the dispute.

/s/ Joseph W. Kim

title: Order Granting Temporary Injunction
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS
160TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. DC-24-11223

TECHNOVANCE SOLUTIONS, INC., Plaintiff
v.
MARGARET HAYNES, Defendant

ORDER GRANTING TEMPORARY INJUNCTION

On this 20th day of November, 2024, came on to be heard Plaintiff’s application for temporary injunction. Plaintiff appeared by and through its attorney, Linda M. Park. Defendant appeared in person and by and through her attorney, Carlos M. Hernandez. After considering the pleadings, evidence, and arguments, the Court finds:

1. Plaintiff has a probable right to recovery on its claim for breach of contract, as the non-compete agreement is likely enforceable under the standard set forth in 
Cedillo v. Gaitan, 264 S.W.3d 351 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2008, no pet.), and 
Peat Marwick Main & Co. v. Haass, 818 S.W.2d 381 (Tex. 1991).
2. Plaintiff will suffer irreparable harm if injunctive relief is not granted, because Defendant may use confidential information to compete unfairly.
3. The Court orders that Defendant, Margaret Haynes (also known as “Maggie” or “Margaret Ellen Haynes”), is immediately restrained from working for any competitor within 50 miles of Technovance’s Houston office, including DataCore Systems LLC, until further order of this Court.

It is further ordered that this temporary injunction shall remain in effect until the final hearing, which is set for January 15, 2025.

The Court sets bond at $10,000, which Plaintiff has posted.

SIGNED this 20th day of November, 2024.

/s/ Judge Patricia A. Nguyen
JUDGE PRESIDING

title: Agreed Final Judgment with Permanent Injunction
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS
224TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-CI-09876

TECHNOVANCE SOLUTIONS, INC., Plaintiff
v.
MARGARET HAYNES (NOW KNOWN AS MARGARET HAYNES-BROWN), Defendant

AGREED FINAL JUDGMENT AND PERMANENT INJUNCTION

On this 5th day of December, 2024, came on for consideration the settlement between Plaintiff Technovance Solutions, Inc. (“Technovance”) and Defendant Margaret Haynes-Brown (formerly known as Margaret Ellen Haynes, and also known as “Maggie” and “M.E.H.”). The parties have agreed to resolve all claims. The Court, having jurisdiction, enters this judgment:

I. RECITALS
1. Defendant Margaret Haynes-Brown (maiden name: Haynes; formerly known as Margaret Ellen Haynes) has agreed to pay Plaintiff the sum of $25,000 as damages, and Plaintiff agrees to release all claims.
2. Defendant agrees to be bound by a permanent injunction for a period of 6 months, prohibiting her from soliciting Plaintiff’s clients and using confidential information.

II. PERMANENT INJUNCTION
3. Defendant, Margaret Haynes-Brown, her agents, and representatives are permanently enjoined from: (a) soliciting any customer of Technovance Solutions, Inc., identified in Exhibit A; (b) disclosing any trade secrets as defined in Texas Business and Commerce Code § 134.001; and (c) working for DataCore Systems LLC, or any similar company, in a role that involves the same responsibilities, for a period of six months.

III. RELEASE
4. Plaintiff releases Defendant from all claims arising out of the employment relationship, except for enforcement of this injunction.

IV. ATTORNEY'S FEES
5. Each party shall bear its own attorney’s fees and costs.

V. FINALITY
6. This is a final judgment. All relief not expressly granted is denied.

SIGNED on the date above.

/s/ Judge Robert L. Martinez
JUDGE PRESIDING

APPROVED:

/s/ Linda M. Park
Attorney for Plaintiff
State Bar No. 24111223

/s/ Carlos M. Hernandez
Attorney for Defendant
State Bar No. 24078456
